title: HM Amit Shah reviews national preparedness for floods and heatwave situations - News On AIR
full_text:
Union Home Minister Amit Shah today reviewed country’s preparedness to deal with potential floods and heat waves in a comprehensive manner. Chairing a high-level meeting in New Delhi, Mr Shah said, there should be an integrated system for flood forecasting at both the Centre and State levels.
He said, at least 60 lakes should be included in the plan to develop an early warning system for 30 high-risk lakes in Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh, Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Arunachal Pradesh, and Sikkim with the support of the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA). Mr Shah said the objective should be to conserve water by constructing check dams on rivers while also minimizing the impact of heat waves. He stressed that efforts should be made to ensure minimum damage to the agriculture sector due to heat waves.
The Minister said, Flood Crisis Management Teams should be constituted and activated in every state of the country. Mr Shah said, the NDMA should conduct a study to assess how many states are following the Ministry of Home Affairs’ directives and the NDMA guidelines for dealing with forest fires, heat waves, and floods. He said, under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, efforts must be made to implement the vision of Zero Casualty Disaster Management.
Mr Shah said that a master plan should be prepared to address the changes in weather patterns caused by climate change and the growing disaster-related challenges arising from them. He also said that weather forecasts and warnings should be disseminated widely and effectively.
The meeting was attended by Union Jal Shakti Minister C. R. Patil, Union Home Secretary, Secretaries and senior officials of various ministries, heads of departments of the National Disaster Management Authority, the Director Generals of the National Disaster Response Force, India Meteorological Department (IMD) and other concerned departments.

title: India's Evening Power Deficit Persists Despite Record Solar Capacity Growth - MarketScale

India's Evening Power Deficit Persists Despite Record Solar Capacity Growth
India's electricity demand exceeded 270 gigawatts on May 22, 2026 amid a heatwave, with a late-evening peak deficit of about 2.57 gigawatts reported by grid regulator Grid-India, according to Reuters. Reuters also reported that as of August 2026, clean energy capacity, led by solar, had surpassed fossil fuel capacity in India for the first time, though coal still supplies roughly 70% of actual generation.

Key takeaways
India's power grid recorded demand above 270 gigawatts on May 22, 2026, during a heatwave, according to Reuters. The same report said the country's late-evening peak deficit reached about 2.57 gigawatts, citing national grid regulator Grid-India, and noted outages in cities including Chennai lasting roughly 40 minutes to an hour. India's power ministry issued a public appeal for consumers to use electricity judiciously during the period, Reuters reported.
Why evenings are the strained period
Reuters reported that daytime electricity demand in India is met partly by solar generation, while evening supply relies heavily on thermal and hydropower sources. Disha Aggarwal, a senior programme lead at the energy think tank CEEW, was quoted by Reuters saying India needs to fast-track battery storage commissioning so surplus solar generation can be used at night. Reuters also reported outages and complaints in New Delhi, Noida, and the state of Odisha during the same heatwave period.
Capacity mix versus generation mix
In an Aug. 17, 2026 commentary, Reuters columnist Gavin Maguire wrote that data from Ember and Global Energy Monitor showed India's clean energy installed capacity had reached 331.7 gigawatts, compared with 302.0 gigawatts of fossil fuel capacity, giving clean power a majority share of installed capacity for the first time. The same commentary noted that coal still accounts for roughly 70% of actual electricity generation because coal plants run continuously while solar output is intermittent. Solar capacity alone stood at 211 gigawatts as of the report, up from 0.07 gigawatts in 2010, per Ember data cited in the column. Between 2025 and mid-2026, India added 75.5 gigawatts of solar capacity compared with 3.8 gigawatts of coal capacity, according to the same Reuters commentary.
Separately, a Bloomberg India Edition newsletter published Aug. 13, 2026 described rising electricity demand in India as tied to climate-driven temperature extremes and growing power use from digital infrastructure, including data centers.
Distribution as a longstanding constraint
A 2014 World Bank diagnostic review of India's power sector said persistent operational and financial shortcomings in electricity distribution represented a core weakness for the sector, noting that revenue for the entire power value chain originates with customers at the distribution level. The report is more than a decade old, but its focus on distribution as the constraint through which new generation and storage capacity must be delivered and billed remains relevant to current discussions of grid reliability.
MarketScale analysis
MarketScale analysis: For companies operating in India with evening-heavy electricity use, the reported gap between installed solar capacity and evening supply reliability may be worth monitoring alongside contract terms for backup power and demand response, though no timeline for closing that gap has been reported.

title: China's Xi in India for BRICS Summit, First Visit Since 2019 - News of Bahrain
full_text:
China's Xi in India for BRICS Summit, First Visit Since 2019
Email: online@newsofbahrain.com
NEW DELHI: Chinese President Xi Jinping arrived in New Delhi on Saturday to attend the 18th BRICS summit.
The Chinese leader landed in the Indian capital at noon local time aboard a special plane.
Xi is attending the high-level meeting of nations at the invitation of Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
The arrival of the delegation was officially reported by Chinese state broadcaster CCTV as leaders gather for the summit.
